profile.name: Henry Nicholls
profile.writeup:
New Zealand's batting depth through the 2010s and 2020s owed a great deal to players who worked quietly in the shadow of bigger names, and Henry Nicholls built one of the more understated careers in that mould. Born in Christchurch and educated at St Andrew's College, the left-handed top-order batter came through Canterbury before a strong run for New Zealand A pushed him into national selection.


Henry's ODI debut came against Sri Lanka in December 2015, followed by a Test debut against Australia at Wellington in February 2016, where he made a half-century but did not immediately hold down a place in the side. A defining moment followed a year later, an unbeaten 145 against England at Eden Park that helped set up a series win and was widely seen as his coming of age at number five. He carried that reliability into the 2019 Cricket World Cup, where New Zealand finished as the runners-up.


It was something of a boom-or-bust period for Nicholls in Test cricket in the years that followed, but there were still some major highlights. He was part of the New Zealand side that won the inaugural World Test Championship final in 2021, before producing one of the finest innings of his career two years later with a double century against Sri Lanka at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. He was then left out of the Test side entirely through 2024, returning only for a tour of Zimbabwe in 2025, where he made an unbeaten 150 in the second Test.


Another lengthy absence followed, before an extraordinary 2025-26 Plunket Shield season forced Nicholls back into contention. He scored 870 runs at an average of 96.66 to finish as the competition's leading run-scorer and helped Canterbury claim another title. The recall came in dramatic circumstances. After Kane Williamson's abrupt mid-series retirement during New Zealand's 2026 tour of England, Nicholls was brought into the side for the second Test at The Oval to fill the No. 3 spot Williamson had occupied for so long. It was a position Nicholls had grown accustomed to playing for Canterbury but had rarely held for New Zealand.


Nicholls made the opportunity count in emphatic fashion, scoring a century on his return to the Test side and playing a key role in New Zealand's victory at The Oval. After such a long spell away from the international setup, Nicholls had not just earned his way back into the side, but had immediately put himself in the conversation to make the No. 3 position his own.
